# Node candidate and published-package acceptance

The published-package workflow requests the central full E2E suite for the exact stable release version. It uses the existing release App and waits for the central result. The retry checks the selected tag against the remote commit. **This is not yet exact-registry acceptance:** the currently available central dispatcher lacks `package-version` and builds the source candidate instead. Central owner review must land and pin an independent registry-install mode with exact-version/integrity evidence, delivery, and cleanup before release rollout.

Acceptance starts only after the gated publisher succeeds. Existing native build and publication checks remain in place. A release-complete Slack message, where configured, is sent only after published-package acceptance; failures remain visible in the workflow summary.

## Candidate PR check

`server-sdk-e2e.yml` uses a trusted `pull_request_target` caller from master. It never checks out or executes PR code with its App token; the central PR runner fetches only the current `refs/pull/N/merge` candidate and executes it inside a disposable container without control-plane/workspace credentials. This applies equally to Release Please and ordinary same-repository PRs; a bot name or branch prefix alone grants no trust. The caller supplies explicit `pr-number` and `merge-sha` inputs to the source-candidate action (the `9bcd97f1b28b1f2c3c7726ccae1bf435f4acf9c4` pin is a review placeholder, not a published action commit); central checks the ref again and the caller rechecks the PR after the completed dispatch. Before rollout, pin an actually published reviewed revision that supports these inputs; the PR check must not be considered operational until then. The trusted aggregate posts the single stable commit **status** `Node Candidate E2E` only to the event merge SHA when it still matches the API-current merge SHA; obsolete runs post no status to the newer candidate. Eligible PRs fail for missing, skipped, failed, cancelled, or stale validation. Fork and Dependabot PRs get this same status with an explicit intentional no-secret success; they do not dispatch E2E. The aggregate job itself runs even when validation is skipped. Existing unit/build checks still apply to those PRs.

## Release candidate gate

Only a published, stable `vX.Y.Z` release tag can start `deploy-npm.yml`; no manual/master-branch publication path exists. `validate-ref` checks the peeled release tag, exact `package.json` version, checked-out source SHA and current master head using gate code from a separate master checkout. It rejects tags predating the gate and published-package workflow; the release and trusted gate checkout SHAs must agree. `sdk-e2e` depends on it and calls the trusted central **full** candidate suite for the release SHA (native delivery, shared contract, receiver negatives, live delivery, and verified pipeline restoration/lock release). `deploy-tag` requires both successes; a parallel master push E2E is not sufficient. After the gate it checks out that same SHA, checks version and master again, builds once, packs `dist/` into a single tarball, records the validated commit and tarball SHA-256 in the run summary, verifies the packed name/version/digest, then publishes **that file** with lifecycle scripts disabled. It rechecks master/tag/version and tarball digest immediately before upload. A branch may still move between that final check and npm upload; no atomic Git/npm lock exists.

This is a **source-commit-bound rebuild**, not a byte-identical artifact handoff. The central candidate workflow builds and tests its own tarball and reports source SHA, suite, request/run identity, result, and its candidate evidence; its tarball is **not** the publication artifact. The npm build can differ byte-for-byte, so checksum equality with the central candidate is neither required nor claimed. The publisher logs the digest of the exact uploaded local file. The separate published-package workflow then exercises the exact public registry version, including delivery and cleanup.

Existing manual publication is disabled. A master-branch dispatch cannot bind the uploaded artifact to a release tag and is no longer a publication path.

## Validation-only retry

1. Open the failed central run from the shared action summary.
2. Resolve the validation failure.
3. Run this workflow at the existing release tag:

```sh
gh workflow run published-sdk-e2e.yml --repo rudderlabs/rudder-sdk-node --ref vX.Y.Z
```

The retry has no upload path or publishing credential. It derives the exact version and commit from the selected tag and checks the tag against the remote before dispatching the published-mode action. It does not use `latest`, publish a package, or recreate a tag. Tags predating this workflow cannot pass the release publisher gate. A validation-only retry needs an existing tag that contains the workflow; an older published tag needs a separately reviewed exact-version acceptance path. Stable `X.Y.Z` versions are supported; prerelease acceptance is not implemented.

A published package remains published if acceptance fails. Do not rerun a successful upload job to retry E2E. A successful validation-only retry does not change an earlier failed run or its notification. Record the new acceptance run in the release ticket and existing Slack release thread.

## Reviewable rollout (not yet enforced)

- [ ] Review [SDK-5973](https://linear.app/rudderstack/issue/SDK-5973) and this caller change separately from the central candidate adapter. Verify central Node `reliability` isolates PR code and `full` on master history performs live delivery **and** verified restoration/cleanup. Keep the existing central interface; pin source candidate action commit `9bcd97f1b28b1f2c3c7726ccae1bf435f4acf9c4` separately from exact-registry action commit `855d3e174e917aab71b93a862c7e74592904d10e`. These illustrative SHAs are not present in the current public action repository; resolve both real commits and verify the central published-mode workflow's exact-version registry install, version/integrity evidence, delivery, and cleanup before merging. A `package-version` input alone does not establish exact registry acceptance.
- [ ] Replace human-authored [PR #502](https://github.com/rudderlabs/rudder-sdk-node/pull/502) via a focused bot-authored draft rather than committing to it. Retain its exact public-registry acceptance and final-notification dependency; merge the replacement only after the central published mode and action pin are reviewed. Do not fire a release for verification.
- [ ] Proposed repository rule for **all** PRs targeting `master`: require exactly `Node Candidate E2E` on the **current PR merge SHA**, not the `pr-gate` job check on master, and do not exempt Release Please, forks or Dependabot by actor. Also keep existing build/unit requirements. This `GITHUB_TOKEN` status is forgeable by another workflow with `statuses: write`, even if a rule selects the GitHub Actions source. Before enforcing the rule, provision a dedicated status publisher unavailable to PR-controlled workflows (for example a scoped GitHub App), verify its actual status source and merge-SHA attachment on same-repo, bot, fork and Dependabot dry-run PRs, then update the gate to use that publisher. Without that owner decision, do not enable the rule or claim this status is a secure required check.
- [ ] Confirm the repository's public-repo event execution policy permits `pull_request_target` before merging: zizmor reports `dangerous-triggers` (high), even though this caller checks out only master and executes PR code solely in the isolated central runner. If policy blocks this event, redesign the trusted caller; do not claim a working PR check or enable the required rule.
- [ ] Verify PR merge-SHA regeneration on base-branch advances: the aggregate fails the API-current SHA if it changes while a run is in flight, but no new PR event is guaranteed just because master advances. Confirm the ruleset invalidates old merge-SHA success and arrange revalidation or a merge-queue hook as needed. Verify check source in Settings before claiming enforcement. Do not change settings as part of this code change.
- [ ] Confirm the `npm-publish` environment exists and allows only published release refs for trusted npm OIDC publishing; verify the npm Trusted Publisher mapping. If not configured, keep rollout draft and do not publish. Central published-mode action inputs were inspected at pin `855d3e…`, but the private central workflow and acceptance behavior cannot be verified anonymously. Validate workflows offline (`node --test`, existing npm tests/build/lint, `actionlint`, `zizmor`) with no central dispatch, release, Slack send or tag creation.

The source-commit rebuild limitation and residual last-check-to-upload branch race remain release evidence caveats, not a claim of byte-for-byte central validation. Hosted acceptance awaits the next normal release.
